display.name: Linear
display.blurb: Query and mutate Linear issues, projects, teams, and comments through its GraphQL API — authenticated with the workspace's OAuth app token, brokered at the egress proxy and never seen by the agent.

cli.doc:
Use `linear` to query and mutate Linear from this session via its GraphQL API. Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects the workspace's Linear OAuth app token (actor=app — actions attribute to the workspace's agent app user) on requests to api.linear.app; `LINEAR_API_KEY` is a managed placeholder. Do NOT set a real key or run any login.

Linear is a GraphQL-only API: ONE endpoint, POST https://api.linear.app/graphql. There is a SINGLE power, `linear:graphql`, which grants both reads and writes (queries and mutations) over that endpoint — read/write cannot be split by path on a GraphQL API.

Subcommands (all run a GraphQL document):
  linear whoami                       Current identity (the `viewer` query) — a quick auth check.
  linear teams                        List your teams (id, key, name).
  linear issues [query]               Search issues by free text (first 25; id, identifier, title, state).
  linear issue <id>                   Fetch one issue by id or identifier (e.g. ENG-123).
  linear projects                     List projects (id, name, state).
  linear comment <issueId> <text>     Add a comment to an issue (a mutation).
  linear create <teamId> <title> [description]   Create an issue (a mutation).
  linear query '<graphql>' [varsJSON] Run an arbitrary query or mutation. Pass variables as a JSON object string.
  linear raw '<json-body>'            POST a raw GraphQL JSON body verbatim.

Examples:
  linear whoami
  linear issues "login bug"
  linear query 'query{ teams{ nodes{ id name } } }'
  linear query 'mutation($t:String!){ issueCreate(input:{teamId:"...",title:$t}){ success issue{ identifier } } }' '{"t":"New bug"}'

Responses are JSON of the form {"data":{...}} or {"errors":[...]}. GraphQL can return HTTP 200 with an `errors` array; a missing/invalid token yields HTTP 401 with extensions.type=authentication_error. All requests need the `linear:graphql` power.
